formulas.name: Insufficient discrimination detection rule (subgroup size n=2)
formulas.expression: If there are not more than 3 possible values for the range within the control limits, then the measurement units are too large for the purposes of the control chart.
formulas.conditions: subgroup size = 2
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Insufficient discrimination detection rule (subgroup size n>=3)
formulas.expression: Idem, but now up to 4 different values.
formulas.conditions: subgroup size >= 3
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: R-chart control limits and borderline condition
formulas.expression: UCL = D4*d2*MU ; LCL = D3*d2*MU ; borderline case sigma = MU gives (n=2) UCL - LCL ~= 3.69*MU ; (n=3) UCL - LCL ~= 4.36*MU
formulas.conditions: E(R) ~= 1.1*sigma for subgroup size n=2; borderline condition is sigma = MU
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Bias and repeatability from reference standard (X-bar/R chart)
formulas.expression: bias = X_bar_bar - ref.value ; repeatability = R_bar / d2

symbols.X_bar_bar: grand average of subgroup means of repeated measurements of the reference standard

formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Determining bias: bias and repeatability
formulas.conditions: based on the X-bar/R-chart data
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Determining bias: t-statistic
formulas.conditions: follows a t-distribution with nu degrees of freedom (the course text literally states 'n degrees of freedom' here, but elsewhere and in the CI formula uses the symbol nu - see ambiguities)
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Confidence interval for the true gauge bias
formulas.expression: bias - sigma_r * d2/(d2* * sqrt(g*m)) * t_(1-alpha/2,nu) <= E(bias) <= bias + sigma_r * d2/(d2* * sqrt(g*m)) * t_(1-alpha/2,nu)

symbols.t_(1-alpha/2,nu): t-distribution quantile with nu degrees of freedom
symbols.alpha: significance level (not numerically specified in the course text)

formulas.conditions: (1-alpha)x100% confidence interval; the gauge bias is significant if zero does not belong to this interval
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Patnaik result for the average squared range
formulas.conditions: P.B. Patnaik result (see A.J. Duncan, Quality control and industrial statistics); d2* and nu depend on m (subgroup size) and g (number of subgroups); tabulated in appendix (tabel MSA.pdf)
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Estimating d2* from chi-square moments
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Average and Range method: model
formulas.expression: X_ijl = X_.j. + X_i.. + X_..l ;  X_..l ~ N(0, sigma)

symbols.X_ijl: measurement l of part j by appraiser i

formulas.conditions: k appraisers each measure n parts r times with the gauge; the parts are representative for the process variation
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Average and Range method: appraiser average
formulas.expression: X_bar_i = (1/nr)*sum_j sum_l X_ijl = X_bar_p + X_i.. + X_bar_bar_r ;  X_bar_bar_r ~ N(0, sigma/sqrt(nr))

symbols.X_bar_i: average measured value by appraiser i over all parts and replications
symbols.X_bar_p: fixed number for the given parts
symbols.X_bar_bar_r: average measurement error over all measurements by appraiser i

formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Average and Range method: part average
formulas.expression: X_bar_j = X_.j. + X_a + X_bar_bar_r ;  X_bar_bar_r ~ N(0, sigma/sqrt(kr))

symbols.X_bar_j: average measured value for part j over all appraisers and replications
symbols.X_a: fixed number for the given appraisers
symbols.X_bar_bar_r: average measurement error over all measurements of part j

formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Average and Range method: average range

symbols.R_bar_bar: average range over all parts and appraisers
symbols.R_ij: range of the r replications for part j by appraiser i

formulas.conditions: X_bar_DIFF = range of the appraiser averages; R_bar_p = range of the part averages (defined but not formalized as an equation on this slide)
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Estimation of EV (repeatability), Average and Range method
formulas.expression: E(R_bar_bar) = d2*sigma  =>  EV = sigma ~= R_bar_bar/d2 = R_bar_bar * K1 ;  K1 = 1/d2

symbols.R_bar_bar: average range over all parts and appraisers
symbols.d2: range-to-sigma constant based on subgroup size = r (number of trials)

formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Estimation of AV (reproducibility), Average and Range method
formulas.expression: E(X_bar_DIFF^2) = d2*^2 * sigma^2(X_bar_i)  =>  sigma^2(X_bar_i) ~= X_bar_DIFF^2/d2*^2 = (X_bar_DIFF*K2)^2  =>  AV = sqrt((X_bar_DIFF*K2)^2 - EV^2/(nr))

symbols.d2*: conversion factor based on 1 subgroup of size k (number of appraisers)

formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Estimation of PV (part variation), Average and Range method
formulas.expression: PV = sqrt((R_bar_p*K3)^2 - EV^2/(kr)) ~= R_bar_p * K3 ;  K3 = 1/d2*

symbols.K3: 1/d2*, based on 1 subgroup of size n (number of parts)

formulas.conditions: if process variation is large compared to equipment variation and the selected parts properly represent process variation, PV simplifies to R_bar_p*K3
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: GRR and TV combination, Average and Range method
formulas.expression: GRR^2 = EV^2 + AV^2 ;  TV^2 = GRR^2 + PV^2 ;  %GRR = GRR/TV x 100%

symbols.%GRR: percent GRR relative to total variation

formulas.conditions: acceptance rule of thumb: %GRR<=10% acceptable; 10%<%GRR<=30% may be acceptable depending on application/cost; 30%<%GRR not acceptable
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: ANOVA method: two-way ANOVA table (without interaction)
formulas.expression: Factor a=appraiser: SSa, df_a=(k-1), MSa=SSa/df_a, Fa=MSa/MSe. Factor p=part: SSp, df_p=(n-1), MSp=SSp/df_p, Fp=MSp/MSe. Error e: SSe, df_e=nk(r-1)+(k-1)(n-1), MSe=SSe/df_e. Total: SST, df=nkr-1
formulas.conditions: reproducibility refers to factors appraiser (traditional) and part (by extension); repeatability refers to the error term; significance of factor appraiser means there is an appraiser bias effect (reproducibility significantly > 0)
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: ANOVA method: EV, AV, PV from mean squares
formulas.expression: EV = sqrt(MSe) ; AV = sqrt((MSa - EV^2)/(nr)) ; PV = sqrt((MSp - EV^2)/(kr))
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: ANOVA method: two-way model without interaction (fitted value and residual)
formulas.expression: X_hat_ij = X_bar_bar + (X_bar_i - X_bar_bar) + (X_bar_j - X_bar_bar) ;  X_ijl - X_hat_ij = X_ijl - X_bar_i - X_bar_j + X_bar_bar

symbols.X_hat_ij: model (fitted) value for appraiser i, part j

formulas.conditions: expected measurement value for a given appraiser i and part j in the two-way ANOVA model without interaction
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: ANOVA method: SST decomposition into MSe and MSa
formulas.expression: MSe = sum_i sum_j sum_l (X_ijl - X_hat_ij)^2 / [nk(r-1) + (n-1)(k-1)] = EV^2 ;  MSa = nr*sum_i(X_bar_i - X_bar_bar)^2 / (k-1) = nr*(AV^2 + EV^2/(nr))
formulas.conditions: consequence of the SST decomposition proof (see also Theoretical background of a GRR study.pdf)
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Proof of SS_T decomposition
formulas.expression: SS_T = sum sum sum (X_ijl - X_bar)^2 = sum sum sum (X_ijl - X_hat_ij)^2 + sum sum sum (X_bar_i - X_bar)^2 + sum sum sum (X_bar_j - X_bar)^2  [cross terms (1),(2),(3) each shown to equal 0]
formulas.conditions: full algebraic proof given, showing cross-product terms (1),(2),(3) vanish
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

formulas.name: Combined standard uncertainty (steel strip example)

symbols.u1: calibration uncertainty of the tape measure
symbols.u4: repeatability uncertainty from the 3 repeated measurements

formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Calculating the uncertainty in the width of a steel strip.pdf

formulas.name: Repeatability uncertainty from range (steel strip example)
formulas.expression: u4 = (R / d2) ... with E(R) = d2*sigma, here u4 = 2 / 1.693

symbols.R: range of the repeated measurements (=2 mm)

formulas.conditions: footnote 5: E(R) = d2*sigma; the repeatability, based on the range, is 2/d2 = 2/1.693
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Calculating the uncertainty in the width of a steel strip.pdf

formulas.name: Result with expanded uncertainty (steel strip example)

symbols.R: range of a sample of X-values
symbols.sigma: std dev of normally distributed X (mean mu)
symbols.d2: constant depending on sample size n
symbols.d3: constant depending on sample size n

formulas.conditions: X normally distributed with mean mu and variance sigma^2; example values given: d2 = 2,326 and d3 = 0,864 for 'a sample of size' (the sample size value itself is missing/omitted in the printed text - see ambiguities)
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Theoretical background of a GRR study.pdf

formulas.name: Mean and variance of a chi-square distribution

symbols.X: random variable following a chi-square distribution

formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Theoretical background of a GRR study.pdf

formulas.name: Distribution of the average squared range
formulas.expression: nu*R_bar^2 / (d2*^2*sigma^2) ~ chi^2(nu) ;  E(nu*R_bar^2/(d2*^2*sigma^2)) = nu  =>  E(R_bar^2) = d2*^2*sigma^2

symbols.R_bar: average range based on g samples (subgroups) of size m
symbols.sigma: std dev of normally distributed X
symbols.nu: degrees of freedom, depends on m and g
symbols.d2*: constant depending on m and g

formulas.conditions: example: for 5 samples of size 3, d2*=1,73857 and nu=9,3; d2* -> d2 as g -> infinity
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Theoretical background of a GRR study.pdf

formulas.name: Calculation of EV (theoretical derivation)
formulas.expression: E(R_bar) = E(R) = d2*sigma = d2*EV  =>  EV = R_bar/d2

symbols.R_bar: average range over all parts and appraisers

formulas.conditions: assumes EV is independent from the appraiser and part
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Theoretical background of a GRR study.pdf

formulas.name: Calculation of AV (theoretical derivation)
formulas.expression: E(X_bar_DIFF^2) = d2*^2*sigma^2(X_bar_i) ;  sigma^2(X_bar_i) = sigma^2(X_i..) + sigma^2(X_bar_r) = AV^2 + sigma^2/(nr) = AV^2 + EV^2/(nr) ;  AV^2 = X_bar_DIFF^2/d2*^2 - EV^2/(nr)

symbols.X_bar_DIFF: range of the appraiser averages X_bar_i
symbols.d2*: conversion factor based on 1 subgroup of size k (number of appraisers)
symbols.X_bar_r: average measurement error for operator i (all parts, all replications)

formulas.conditions: for the average measurement X_bar_i of operator i (all parts n and replications r): X_bar_i = X_bar_p + X_i.. + X_bar_r
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Theoretical background of a GRR study.pdf

formulas.name: Calculation of TV and %GRR (theoretical derivation)
formulas.expression: TV^2 = PV^2 + GRR^2 = PV^2 + AV^2 + EV^2 ;  %GRR = GRR/TV
formulas.conditions: PV calculated in the same way as AV
formulas.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Theoretical background of a GRR study.pdf

constant_tables.name: Values associated with the Distribution of the Average Range (degrees of freedom nu and conversion factor d2* by number of subgroups g and subgroup size m)
constant_tables.note: Each data cell is formatted as 'nu/d2*' where nu (1st line in the printed table) is the degrees of freedom and d2* (2nd line) is the conversion factor, for g subgroups (rows, number of subgroups 1-20) of subgroup size m (columns 2-20). The last row gives d2 (=d2* as g->infinity) and cd (constant difference, used to build up additional values of nu), transcribed as 'd2/cd'. Source note printed on the table: 'Table entries: 1st line of each cell is the degrees of freedom (nu) and the 2nd line of each cell is d2*; d2 is the infinity value of d2*. Additional values of nu can be built up from the constant difference cd.' 'Note: The notation used in this table follows that of Acheson Duncan Quality Control and Industrial Statistics, 5th edition, McGraw-Hill, 1986.' Formula printed under table: nu*(R_bar/d2*)^2/sigma^2 is distributed approximately as a chi-square distribution with nu degrees of freedom where R_bar is the average range of g subgroups of size m. Source: 'Measurement Systems Analysis', Reference Manual, (c) DaimlerChrysler Corporation, Ford Motor Company, General Motors Corporation, 2002.

given.context: Cold Rolling Mill dept of a steel plant, width of steel coils measured with a tape measure at entrance of galvanizing line

given.u1_calibration: u1 = 1834 x 0.1% / 2 = 0.917 (calibration certificate: uncertainty 0.1% of reading at coverage factor 2, normal distribution)
given.u2_resolution: u2 = 0.5 / sqrt(3) = 0.289 (tape divisions are millimetres; reading to nearest division gives error <= 0.5 mm, uniformly distributed)
given.u3_perpendicularity: u3 = 0.917 / sqrt(3) = 0.529 (tape lies straight but not always perpendicular to the coil, overestimate ~0.1% assumed uniformly distributed; correction of -1.8 mm to be subtracted)
given.u4_repeatability: u4 = 2 / d2 = 2 / 1.693 = 0.682 (repeatability based on the range of the 3 measurements; d2 for subgroup size 3 = 1.693; footnote: E(R) = d2*sigma)
given.type_of_estimates: u1, u2, u3 are type B estimates; u4 is a type A estimate

conventions.as_stated: The course teaches both methods ('Determining repeatability and reproducibility: Average and range method' p34-35, and '...Anova' p36-37) and states ANOVA 'offers more accurate estimates for repeatability and reproducibility' and can be extended to different components of reproducibility and to interactions. The worked exercise (GRR - ANOVA - average and range - 2.xlsx) applies both methods to the identical steering-mechanism dataset: %GRR = 49.47% (ANOVA, sheet '2way anova') vs %GRR = 50.01% (average & range, sheet 'ranges'). No single method is declared mandatory in this slice.
conventions.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

conventions.topic: K1/K2/K3 (or d2*) constants used, and which trials/operators/parts counts
conventions.as_stated: K1 = 1/d2, with d2-value based on subgroup size = r (the number of trials/replications). K2 = 1/d2*, with d2* based on 1 subgroup of size k (the number of appraisers). K3 = 1/d2*, based on 1 subgroup of size n (the number of parts). In the worked exercise ('ranges' sheet): d2 = 1.12838 for subgroup size 2 (r=2 replications), d2*(A) = 1.91155 for '1 subgroup van grootte 3' (k=3 appraisers), d2*(P) = 2.48124 for '1 subgroup van grootte 5' (n=5 parts) - these match the g=1 row of the 'tabel MSA' d2*/nu table at m=3 and m=5 respectively.
conventions.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

conventions.as_stated: Footnote on slide 24: 'Historically, by convention, a 99 % spread has been used to represent the “full spread of the measurement error”. Following this convention, a multiplying factor of 5.15 has to be used. More recently a multiplying factor of 6 is used, representing 99.73 % spread.' The formulas actually printed on the slides (%GRR = 6*sigma_m/6*sigma_o and %GRR = 6*sigma_m/TOL) use the factor 6, not 5.15.
conventions.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

conventions.topic: %GRR relative to total variation vs relative to tolerance
conventions.as_stated: Both bases are taught: '%GRR based on process variation' = 6*sigma_m/6*sigma_o (x100%) and '%GRR based on tolerance range' = 6*sigma_m/TOL (x100%) (slide 24). Separately, the average-range and ANOVA method sections define %GRR = GRR/TV x 100% i.e. relative to total variation TV (slide 35), and this is the basis actually used in both worked-example spreadsheets (2way anova sheet: %GRR = sqrt((EV^2+AV^2)/TV^2); ranges sheet: same formula).
conventions.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

conventions.as_stated: Rule of thumb (slide 35): '%GRR <= 10% : gauge generally considered to be acceptable'; '10% < %GRR <= 30% : gauge may be acceptable based upon importance of application, cost of procurement, cost of repair, etc'; '30% < %GRR : gauge considered to be not acceptable – every effort should be made to improve the measurement system.' Slide 23 similarly states measurements are 'often characterized as inadequate when sigma_GRR is above some percentage of the tolerance interval (commonly 20 % or 30 %)'. In the worked exercise both methods give %GRR ~ 49-50%, i.e. > 30%, so the workbook's own conclusion cell literally reads 'niet geschikt' (not suitable).
conventions.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

conventions.topic: one- vs two-tailed defaults (bias/linearity significance tests)
conventions.as_stated: The bias test uses an explicitly two-sided formulation: '(1 - alpha) x 100 % confidence interval for the true gauge bias' with 'The gauge bias is significant if zero does not belong to this interval' (slide 32), i.e. a two-sided test. The linearity test is stated as 'H0: slope = 0 vs HA: slope <> 0' (two-sided) and, if accepted, an additional two-sided test 'H0: intercept = 0 vs HA: intercept <> 0' (slide 33). No numeric alpha value is given anywhere in this slice for either test; alpha remains symbolic.
conventions.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

conventions.topic: Gage R&R (ANOVA) method: pooling the operator x part interaction when not significant
conventions.as_stated: The course PDF (pages 34-38) does not state a numeric alpha threshold for pooling the interaction term in the ANOVA method. However, the lecturer's own worked-solution spreadsheet ('2way anova' sheet) computes a 'derived ANOVA table, without estimation of the interaction (additive model)' (Dutch label: 'Afgeleide ANOVA-tabel, zonder schatting van de interactie (additief model)') in which the Interaction SS (P-value = 0.29389593285256765, i.e. not significant at common alpha levels) is pooled together with the original Within/error SS into a new 'Within' term with df = 23, and EV/AV/PV are computed from this pooled table. No explicit pooling-alpha criterion (e.g. 0.25) is stated in the course text itself; this is only implicit in the workbook.

conventions.topic: rounding of the data ('afgeronde data' vs 'originele data')
conventions.as_stated: The Rheostat Knob Data workbook deliberately provides the same 27 subgroups of 5 measurements both 'The original data recorded in inches to 1/1000 inch' (sheet 'originele data') and 'Rounded data to 1/100 inch' (sheet 'afgeronde data'), specifically to illustrate the effect of coarse measurement resolution (inadequate discrimination) on the appearance of an X-bar/R control chart (course text, slide 30: 'Illustration : Rheostat knob data'). This is a teaching illustration of measurement unit granularity, not a general data-rounding convention for calculations elsewhere in the course.
conventions.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

conventions.as_stated: Neither the 'Determining bias' (slide 32) nor the 'Determining linearity' (slide 33) sections specify a numeric significance level; both are given only in symbolic form ('(1-alpha)x100%' / 'H0 ... vs HA ...'). The course is silent on which numeric alpha to use for these MSA tests.
conventions.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

conventions.as_stated: The lecturer's own workbook ('2way anova' sheet) uses Excel's built-in 'Anova: Two-Factor With Replication' data-analysis output (SUMMARY table with Count/Sum/Average/Variance, and ANOVA table with SS/df/MS/F/P-value/F crit), plus explicit formulas '=_xlfn.F.DIST(N43,L43,L45,TRUE)' and '=_xlfn.F.INV(0.95,L43,L45)' for the derived (pooled) ANOVA table, and SQRT()/SUM()/MAX()/MIN() for EV/AV/PV/TV/%GRR. The 'on d2 and d2star' sheet uses volatile '=_xlfn.NORM.INV(RAND(),0,1)' and OFFSET() formulas for its Monte-Carlo demonstration.

conventions.topic: ndc (number of distinct categories) formula and minimum
conventions.as_stated: Not present anywhere in this slice's source material (main MSA primer pdf, GRR workbook, Rheostat workbook, or the two short PDFs). No ndc formula or minimum-value criterion is stated in these documents; per instructions, no value is inferred.
conventions.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

ambiguities.issue: Slide text for the bias t-statistic literally states the statistic 'follows a t-distribution with n degrees of freedom', but the same slide's confidence-interval formula and surrounding text (and the Patnaik result on the same page) consistently use the symbol nu (not n) for the (possibly non-integer) degrees of freedom, and n is used elsewhere in the document for 'number of parts'. Transcribed as printed; likely an inconsistency/typo in the course text between 'n' and 'nu'.
ambiguities.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Black Belt in Six Sigma - Measurement System Analysis.pdf

ambiguities.issue: 'Theoretical background of a GRR study.pdf' states: 'For instance for a sample of size d2 = 2,326 and d3 = 0,864.' The sentence appears to be missing the actual sample size value n (grammatically expected, e.g. 'for a sample of size n=5'). Based on standard d2 tables (d2=2.326 corresponds to n=5), the missing value is very likely 5, but this is not printed in the source and is not filled in per the no-inference rule.
ambiguities.file: source/course/Les 5/20260619_ottoy_Theoretical background of a GRR study.pdf

ambiguities.issue: The 'tabel MSA.pdf' page is an image-only scan of a large two-line-per-cell table (nu on line 1, d2* on line 2) for g=1..20 subgroups x m=2..20 subgroup size, transcribed visually at 400 dpi. Digits were legible in the rendered crops used for transcription, but because the whole table (400+ numeric cells) was read from a scanned image rather than a text layer, any single-digit misread (e.g. a smudged 1/7 or 3/8) cannot be fully ruled out; spot cross-checks against the same constants reproduced in 'GRR - ANOVA - avegage and range - 2.xlsx' (d2=1.12838 for m=2; d2*=1.91155 for g=1,m=3; d2*=2.48124 for g=1,m=5) and against 'Theoretical background of a GRR study.pdf' (d2*=1.73857, nu=9.3 for g=5,m=3) were consistent with the transcribed table.

Worked example S10-WE05 (linearity.txt) and S10-WE06 (Cp/%GRR=50% exercise, slide 24) and S10-WE08 (Gauge Performance Curve numeric example, slide 27) are exercises/questions posed to the student; the course source does not print a computed numeric answer for any of them (they are left as exercises). Recorded with empty stated_answers as instructed.

ambiguities.issue: The 'on d2 and d2star' sheet of the GRR workbook (~600 rows) is a Monte-Carlo simulation using volatile formulas (RAND()/NORM.INV/OFFSET); its cell values are not fixed data and change every time the workbook recalculates. It was summarised (topic + structure) rather than transcribed as a constant table, per the task instructions for a non-constant large sheet.
